one_line_contribution: Segment GEPA-optimized prompts into typed atomic clauses, causally estimate each clause's contribution both on its source task (deletion) and on seven other tasks (insertion) to build a clause x target portability matrix, and use it to claim a dissociation — source contribution does not predict transfer, clause type does — cashed out as a zero-rollout portable-clause library priced in cold-start GEPA rollouts.
closest_prior_work: Three works threaten different halves. (1) ContextCite (Cohen-Wang et al., 2024) already estimates causal contributions of individual context segments by random ablation plus a linear surrogate over presence indicators — that is Experiment (4b) essentially verbatim; the methodological contribution is therefore a reapplication, not a new estimator, and the proposal never cites it. (2) Battle & Gollapudi, 'The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Eccentric Automatic Prompts' (2024), reports that optimizer-discovered prompt text is idiosyncratic to the task and executor and does not carry over — which is the proposal's Prediction (c) for content clauses already in the literature, and also predicts that the portable residue will be small enough to be swallowed by the filler/sham controls. (3) Bsharat et al., 'Principled Instructions Are All You Need' (2024), is a hand-written, empirically evaluated generic instruction checklist (output contracts, edge-case handling, decomposition) — i.e., Baseline (iii) already exists as a published artifact, so if the harvested library merely matches it the paper reduces to a replication with a negative result. The proposal's stated foils (SPoT/ATTEMPT, OPRO, APE, MIPROv2) are correctly dismissed as monolithic or soft-prompt, but they are the easy foils; the hard ones above are unaddressed.
strongest_objection: The central dissociation (Prediction b) is confounded by construction, because the two correlated quantities are measured in incomparable regimes. Source contribution comes from Experiment (4): deleting a clause from a fully optimized prompt in which every other optimized clause is still present. Cross-task contribution comes from Experiment (5): inserting that clause into the target's bare baseline prompt. Prompt gains are strongly submodular — a clause deleted from a saturated optimized prompt shows a small marginal effect because its function is redundantly covered, while the same clause dropped into an unoptimized baseline with full headroom shows a large one. A low Spearman correlation between a deletion-from-saturated estimate and an insertion-into-empty estimate is the expected signature of headroom and redundancy asymmetry alone, and would be obtained even if every clause were perfectly domain-general. Attenuation correction does not touch this; it corrects for unreliability, not for a systematic context difference. Worse, the same confound loads the effect onto clause type in the predicted direction for a second, non-empirical reason: output-contract and error-avoidance clauses are exactly the clauses a bare baseline prompt lacks, while task-specific-content clauses are, by the taxonomy's own definition, statements about the source domain, so inserting 'identify the bridge entity linking the two supporting passages' into GSM8K is a straw-man manipulation whose failure is analytic rather than discovered. Predictions (a) and (c) are therefore close to entailed by the seven-way labeling scheme, and a reviewer will say the headline finding is a restatement of the taxonomy. Secondary but also sinking: the title claims 'Prompt Optimizers' while only one optimizer (a GEPA reimplementation) is run, so nothing licenses the plural; and the eight generalization units are not eight domains — two BBH clusters and two Super-NaturalInstructions clusters are format siblings, so leave-one-target-out folds leak suite conventions and will inflate measured portability without a within-suite vs cross-suite split.
what_would_fix_it: Make the two attribution regimes symmetric before correlating them: measure each clause's source contribution by insertion into its own task's baseline prompt (matching Experiment 5's operation exactly), and/or measure cross-task contribution by insertion into the target's own GEPA-optimized prompt, and pre-register Prediction (b) on the matched pair. Report the deletion-vs-insertion gap explicitly as a redundancy measure — it is a real finding and it is the thing currently masquerading as the dissociation. Second, gate the dissociation on the domain-scrubbed condition rather than leaving scrubbing as an ablation: if the effect survives after source-domain nouns are stripped and a leakage probe cannot recover the source task, it is empirical; if it does not, the paper should say the dissociation is definitional. Third, run MIPROv2 or a second optimizer family on at least three tasks, or retitle to a single-optimizer claim. Fourth, fix Prediction (c): '>=15% of content-clause x target cells negative beyond the noise floor' is a selection-on-noise statistic that conflicts with the proposal's own admission that per-cell MDE is ~4 points, so it must be paired with the symmetric count of positive cells beyond the floor and an FDR correction, otherwise both counts will be nonzero by construction. Fifth, split the leave-one-target-out results into within-suite and cross-suite folds. Sixth, actually run the preprint search.
missing_baseline: An LLM-abstraction baseline with zero causal measurement: hand the reflector model the seven source tasks' final optimized prompts and ask it to write a generic, domain-stripped prefix of matched token length. This is the arm that decides whether the ~336k-generation attribution apparatus earns its cost. Baseline (iii), the hand-written checklist, tests only whether harvesting from optimizer output was necessary; it does not test whether *causal portability estimation* was necessary, and the proposal's own hypothesis — that a cheap type label predicts transfer better than measured source contribution does — implies that cheap label-based or LLM-summarized selection may match the measured library. For the same reason, type-label-only selection (choose all output-contract and error-avoidance clauses, no portability measurement) belongs in the headline comparison in Experiment (7), not buried as a single-type ablation. Also absent: a target-task-agnostic exemplar baseline, i.e. the best source prompt's exemplar clauses alone, which is the arm practitioners would actually try first.
preprint_collision: Absent, and the omission is disqualifying rather than neutral. The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens with '(All citations unverified; literature search backend was unavailable.)' — so the submission contains zero evidence that anyone looked for recent work, on a topic where prompt-component ablation, prompt-segment attribution, and reusable generic prompt prefixes are all active arXiv areas. Specific likely collisions the authors must clear: ContextCite-style random-ablation attribution over prompt/context segments (the exact estimator in 4b); the 'eccentric automatic prompts' line showing optimizer-discovered text is task- and model-idiosyncratic (pre-empts Prediction c); published hand-written generic instruction checklists such as the 26-principles work (pre-empts Baseline iii and possibly the whole library); and the growing set of GEPA/MIPRO follow-up preprints on warm-starting and cross-task prompt reuse, at least one of which is likely to have reported instruction-skeleton reuse budget curves. I cannot verify from here which of these has already published the clause x target matrix specifically, and that is precisely the problem: the proposal asks the reviewer to take its novelty on faith. Novelty is scored as not established, not as absent.
